documentation.title: Large sliding on a loaded interface: everything moves, nothing changes
documentation.description:
The first FORCE-CARRYING testcase in the suite with slidingType="large", and the gate on the two mechanisms that only run in that combination.
It is the ContactMortarPatch2d model unchanged -- non-matching interface meshes, nu = 0 so the exact contact pressure is the applied 1e6 Pa everywhere -- with slidingType="large". That switches on three things a small-sliding pair never does:
1. the pairing is re-projected onto the DEFORMED primary surface once per Newton iteration; 2. the mortar sub-cell partition is re-cut against the deformed primary outlines on every one of those re-projections; 3. the matrix sparsity pattern is reserved for the whole reference-configuration candidate set, so the pairing may move without leaving the graph, at the cost of assembler elements that carry no points and assemble an exact zero.
The interface here is FLAT and the sliding is nil, so all three must be exactly inert. That is the assertion, and it is a strong one precisely because the answer is known analytically and independently: every number is identical to ContactMortarPatch2d's, to the last digit reported -- maxPressure 1e6, totalContactForce 2e6, minGap -pressure/eps_N, and the partition and pairing counts unchanged.
numContactElements is the load-bearing one for mechanism 3: the element list holds more entries than that, so this number is right only if the reporting counts elements that CARRY POINTS rather than the length of the list. Getting it wrong would break ContactSlidingRamp2d's re-pairing assertion. numReservedElements is the direct evidence that the reservation happened at all, and is zero for every other contact testcase, because a pair that does not slide has nothing to reserve for.
What this testcase does NOT do is judge the geometric tangent. It cannot: the interface is flat, so small-sliding kinematics are exact on it. It is the "changes nothing" half of the evidence; the "changes the right thing" half is ContactSlidingRamp2d (the pairing) and ContactSlidingMortar2d (the partition).
